title: dedicated-autoscaler-burst-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Evelyn Cho
description: Motivation: Improve Dedicated fleet autoscaler behavior under bursty load and provide clearer utilization reporting for SRE/customer dashboards. This PR implements token-bucket smoothing for burst allowance, adds throughput guarantee hooks to the autoscaler, and enriches utilization reporting (per-fleet and per-allocator) used by Redwood Console and billing. Changes include runtime controls for smoothing windows, a new telemetry shim to expose burst headroom, and backfill logic to avoid rapid scale-down after short spikes. Checklist: - [x] Token-bucket smoothing algorithm + tests - [x] Autoscaler throughput guarantee integration - [x] Utilization reporting + metrics + dashboard query examples - [x] API for configuring burst policies per-dedicated-fleet - [x] Documentation and release notes - [x] E2E smoke run on staging Summary of changes: - Autoscaler: add tokenbucket_smoothing that introduces a configurable smoothing_time_s (default 60s) and decay factor to spread burst consumption over a window so short spikes don't immediately consume burst quota. - Throughput guarantees: new autoscaler hook that reserves a small steady-state capacity percentage when a fleet is configured with throughput_guarantee_percent; integrates with token bucket to ensure guaranteed capacity isn't consumed by burst. - Reporting: new metrics exported via /metrics and internal event stream: dedicated_fleet_burst_headroom, dedicated_fleet_utilization_aggregated, allocator_utilization_percentile_p95. Console: updated dashboard queries and example alerts (high sustained utilization, low burst headroom). Backwards compatibility: existing configs continue to work; new config keys are optional. See docs/operational/autoscaler.md for examples and recommended defaults. Performance: microbenchmarks show 8-12% reduction in scale-down churn in synthetic spike workloads and no measurable increase in average latency. Rollout plan: - Canary on 2 test fleets in us-west-2 for 48h - Gradual rollout to Dedicated beta fleets - Monitor dedicated_fleet_burst_headroom and autoscaler_scale_events for regressions Related: ENG-1248 (priority routing), ENG-1304 (utilization reporting), SUP-8421 (customer incident escalations where fleets scaled down too aggressively).

review_comments: Marcus Li: Overall looks good. A couple of concerns: (1) tokenbucket default decay 0.6 seems aggressive for long-running spikes — can we make it config-driven? (2) we need a clear migration path for fleets with custom scaling policies.
Evelyn Cho: replied to Marcus Li — made decay configurable (config/schema.yaml) and added migration guidance in docs/operational/autoscaler.md. Also added tests for long-running spike scenarios.
Asha Patel: Can you add a small benchmark measuring the extra CPU used by the smoothing logic? We saw a small increase in telemetry CPU in a prior PR.

Evelyn Cho: added microbenchmarks and included results in the PR description; results show <2% CPU overhead in synthetic workloads. Also added an optional telemetry sampling flag to reduce metric cardinality.
Diego Ramirez: LGTM after addressing comments; left one nit about alert thresholds in alerts.yml.
Evelyn Cho: adjusted alert thresholds and pushed a follow-up commit.
ci_checks: ci/e2e — failed on first run (flaky test autoscaler_burst_smoothing), reran — passed
release_notes: Enhancements to Dedicated autoscaler: token-bucket smoothing to reduce scale-down churn during short spikes, throughput guarantee integration to reserve steady-state capacity, and enriched utilization reporting (dedicated_fleet_burst_headroom, allocator_util_p95). Default smoothing window: 60s. No breaking changes; new config options are optional.
notes_for_ops: Canary plan: enable feature on 2 non-production fleets in us-west-2 for 48h. Watch metrics: dedicated_fleet_burst_headroom, autoscaler_scale_events, allocator_util_p95. If sustained unexpected scale events occur, roll back by disabling tokenbucket_smoothing or setting tokenbucket_smoothing.time_s=0.
post_merge_tasks: Notify Dedicated beta users via release notes
qa_summary: QA ran e2e synthetic spike scenarios with bursts of 200% traffic for 30s/90s/300s. Results: smoothing prevents immediate burst quota exhaustion for 30s spikes, throughput_guarantee_percent reserved capacity remained stable under mixed traffic. One flaky test fixed by increasing test waiting window.
